record.paper_title: Twenty open problems in quantum control
record.original_question: How does noise in the time-dependent control Hamiltonian H(t) affect the fidelity of a quantum-control protocol, and can noise in the Hamiltonian that applies control be handled by the same methods used to handle noise in the auxiliary controller?

evidence.quote: The system and auxiliary evolve under a time-dependent Hamiltonian H(t), whose purpose is solely to control the evolution of S.
Problem 16: How does noise on the control Hamiltonian H(t) affect the fidelity? Can noise on the auxiliary and noise on the Hamiltonian be managed in the same way?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a finite-dimensional quantum system S coupled to an auxiliary quantum system A, with combined Hilbert space H = H_S ⊗ H_A. The joint evolution is governed by a time-dependent control Hamiltonian H(t) acting on H, whose role is to steer the evolution of S so as to implement a target unitary (or, more generally, a target completely positive trace-preserving map) U_target on S with high fidelity. Given an initial state ρ(0) on H, the realized evolution is the unitary propagator U(T) = T exp(-i ∫_0^T H(t) dt), and the achieved fidelity is measured by some standard fidelity functional F(U(T), U_target).

Suppose now that two independent sources of noise are present:
(i) noise on the auxiliary system A (e.g. stochastic perturbations of A's free Hamiltonian, or coupling of A to an external bath, modeled by a Lindblad dissipator L_A acting on A); and
(ii) noise on the control Hamiltonian itself, modeled by replacing H(t) with H(t) + δH(t), where δH(t) is a stochastic operator-valued process (for instance Gaussian white noise on the control amplitudes, multiplicative noise on each control field, or pulse-shape distortion).

Provide a quantitative analysis of the following:

1. Derive an expression (or rigorous bounds) for the expected loss of fidelity E[1 - F(U(T), U_target)] as a functional of the statistical properties (mean, covariance, spectral density) of δH(t), for a given control protocol H(t).

2. Determine whether noise of type (ii) on the control Hamiltonian can be suppressed or compensated by the same techniques (e.g. dynamical decoupling, optimal-control robustification, filter-function methods, decoherence-free subspaces, quantum error correction on the auxiliary) that are used to handle noise of type (i) on the auxiliary system, and characterize the regimes (noise spectrum, control bandwidth, protocol duration T) in which such a unified treatment is possible or provably impossible.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as one of twenty open problems in quantum control and remains open in the general form stated. While there is extensive literature on robust optimal control, filter functions, and dynamical decoupling addressing control-field noise, no comprehensive resolution unifying control-Hamiltonian noise with auxiliary-system noise has been established. No source confirms a definitive solution.

status_evidence.title: Twenty open problems in quantum control (arXiv:1304.0819)
status_evidence.snippet: Lists open problems including the effect of noise on the control Hamiltonian and whether it can be handled like noise on the auxiliary.
status_evidence.claim: The question is presented as an open problem in the field of quantum control.
